Optional refinement for the editor: the source states stress is 'non-distinctive and predictable.. fixed on the final syllable' with no exceptions mentioned, which would support strict fixed: final syllable rather than 'fixed-dominant' (not in the strict set) if the non-strict flag was set only for want of an explicit no-exceptions statement; stress domain w.r.t. clitics is not stated in JIPA, so 'domain' stays not yet coded pending Kruspe 2010.

sources.citation: Kruspe & Hajek 2009, Mah Meri, JIPA 39(2), section 'Stress and syllable weight' (Cambridge Core, doi:10.1017/S0025100309003946)
sources.quote: Word-level stress is non-distinctive and predictable: it is fixed on the final syllable which in turn is always bimoraic (heavy).

sources.citation: Kruspe, Nicole & John Hajek. 2009. Mah Meri. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 39(2): 241-248. doi:10.1017/S0025100309003946 (open access on Cambridge Core).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Word-level stress is non-distinctive and predictable: it is fixed on the final syllable which in turn is always bimoraic (heavy), e.g. /luˈwat/ 'mangrove worm'. As a result, stressed final vowels in open syllables are lengthened – they are usually fully long, but can also appear optionally as semi-long.
